papers.abstract: Predicting the transient nonlinear responses of complex engineering structures remains challenging due to large finite element meshes, heterogeneous structural components, and history-dependent mechanical behavior. This study proposes a topology-prior-guided regional latent dynamics (TPLD) surrogate model that combines physically structured regional representations with dynamics-aware latent learning for full-field time-history prediction. Based on mesh topology and engineering priors, structural responses are encoded into spatially coupled regional latent variables through region-aware feature extraction and topology-constrained interactions. An auxiliary one-step prediction task enhances latent-space dynamical predictability by introducing state-transition supervision. A load-conditioned spatiotemporal Mamba model then predicts regional latent trajectories by integrating temporal causal scanning and bidirectional spatial scanning, while a shared coordinate-conditioned decoder reconstructs full-field nodal responses. The framework is evaluated on three finite element datasets: a parametric stiffened panel, a partitioned pressure impact plate, and a Toyota Yaris full-vehicle crash model. The relative L2 errors for the three displacement components range from 4.00% to 8.21% on the stiffened panel and from 1.41% to 12.22% on the approximately 1.49-million-node vehicle model. On the BIW crash benchmark, TPLD achieves a relative L2 position error of 0.620%, representing a 30.7% reduction compared with the best-performing GeoTransolver configuration. Ablation studies demonstrate the advantages of topology-guided regional representations over global latent and learnable soft-slice alternatives, while auxiliary one-step prediction particularly improves the prediction of accumulated plastic strain.

papers.title: MirrorGuard: Defending LiDAR Perception against Passive Mirror Attacks
papers.abstract: Mirror-based LiDAR attacks passively redirect automotive LiDAR's beams to create phantom objects in the vehicle perception. Recent work has demonstrated that these attacks may cause vehicles to brake for a phantom where nothing stands. Every phantom return is a genuine time-of-flight measurement, so current spoofing defenses are not able to differentiate phantoms from real objects. We present MirrorGuard, a physics-informed defense that identifies and removes mirror-induced phantom returns before they affect downstream perception. MirrorGuard tests three consequences of the reflected path. Every phantom bearing crosses the mirror's finite aperture, its opaque surface blocks any direct return beyond it, and the two reflections off the mirror dim the phantom. MirrorGuard identifies a phantom by these cues over multiple scans and removes the reflected beams before it reaches any detector or occupancy grid. On real-world recordings of this attack, MirrorGuard removes 96.31% of the phantom's returns at 98.30% precision, with 99.99% of non-phantom returns untouched. In a closed loop with the CARLA driving simulator and the open-source stack (Autoware), a vehicle without the defense halts for an obstacle that is not present and a following car crashes into its rear. With MirrorGuard, no vehicle produces a halt or a crash. MirrorGuard runs at 59 ms mean per scan on a CPU and is a software-only solution that does not require new hardware or environmental training.

papers.title: Beyond Which: Where, How, and When in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically rely on vision-language model (VLM) features as the primary perceptual source for action prediction, showing strong generalization across diverse robotic manipulation tasks. Although VLM features can identify which entities are relevant to action prediction, precise manipulation also requires understanding where task-relevant entities are located within the spatial layout, how their geometric structure constrains physical interaction, and when spatial or geometric information should make a greater contribution to action prediction. To this end, we introduce {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA to organize VLA perception and action prediction around which, where, how, and when. Specifically, {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA retains VLM-based semantic entity perception which and further introduces spatial distance perception where and geometric structure perception how with adaptive spatial-geometric guidance when to enrich the perceptual information available for action prediction. Experiments across real-world settings and simulation benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA.

papers.title: Uncovering Separable and Composable Skill Mechanisms in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent work has sought to localize the internal mechanisms underlying visual reasoning skills in vision-language models. These methods largely overlook separability and composability in both mechanism identification and evaluation. We propose separability and composability as two important desiderata for skill localization. Separability requires identified mechanisms to contribute primarily to their target skills while having limited effects on other skills, enabling precise diagnosis and targeted intervention. Composability requires skill mechanisms to be combinable to support complex tasks, allowing a small set of mechanisms to account for broader capabilities. In this work, we propose a multi-skill interpretability framework DISCO, built around these two properties. For identification, we propose Separable Head Selection, which selects skill-specific attention heads based on their contributions across skills. For evaluation, we are the first to design metrics for measuring separability and composability of identified heads. Extensive experiments on three VLMs and four fundamental visual reasoning skills demonstrate the effectiveness of DISCO. It achieves the highest separability, outperforming the strongest baseline by 24.80, 18.38, and 13.75 points across the three models, respectively, while also achieving the highest composability on all three models.

papers.title: Temporal Leakage Distorts the TGB Node Affinity Leaderboard: A Point-in-Time Audit
papers.abstract: Node affinity prediction in the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB) asks how a node's future interactions will be distributed over other nodes. On this task, methods that reuse past ground-truth labels often outperform temporal graph neural networks, and the state of the art builds on them. Such comparisons assume a point-in-time correct evaluation, in which a model receives only information available at prediction time. Drawing on as-of joins and bitemporal databases, we formalize this requirement by distinguishing when a label must be predicted, its query time, from when it is fully determined, its availability time, and we audit the four TGB node affinity datasets and their evaluation loop with model-agnostic tools. None of the four meets it. On three datasets, each label summarizes a single day about five days after its timestamp, not the documented following week, yet the loop feeds it back right after that timestamp; on the fourth, the loop processes the edges from which each label is computed before predicting it. Under a drop-in leakage-free protocol, every method whose inputs leak loses up to 17% of its NDCG@10, the advantage of past labels over the interaction stream nearly vanishes or reverses, and both the best configuration of the state of the art and the rankings change; a blend of training-free long-memory statistics, with weights fit on validation data, matches or exceeds the state of the art under both protocols. Point-in-time correctness should therefore be built into benchmarks, and our tools carry over to other benchmarks whose labels aggregate event streams over time windows.

papers.title: Face Is Not All You Need: MIME Benchmark for Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) is a fundamental task in multimedia understanding, where state-of-the-art methods have achieved prominent success relying on the assumption of complete, well-aligned multimodal inputs. However, real-world unconstrained scenarios often suffer from unpredictable modality degradation and information loss, leading to catastrophic performance collapse of existing MER models that heavily depend on facial cues as the core inference anchor. However, few systematic works evaluate model robustness under diverse, fine-grained incomplete settings, as prior works are limited to coarse-grained full-modality removal and neglect interpretable analysis of emotional reasoning. To bridge this gap, we formally define the Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Recognition (IMER) task, which benchmarks model generalization and robustness under multi-grained modality and emotional information loss. We further construct MIME, a dedicated IMER benchmark with 2,000 video segments covering realistic fine-grained facial-detail degradation, severe facial degradation, and extreme full-modality loss, surpassing the limited coarse-grained settings of prior works. We also propose the Chain of Emotion (CoE) analysis paradigm with tailored metrics to dissect the fine-grained emotional cue perception and reasoning process of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Extensive experiments on seven mainstream MLLMs reveal that body language and scene context act as critical compensatory mechanisms under facial degradation, while a pronounced gap exists between models' basic visual perception ability and high-level cognitive reasoning. Our work provides a focused evaluation platform and actionable insights for advancing robust multimodal emotion recognition. Our dataset and code are public at https://yuxinokk.github.io/MIME.

papers.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
papers.abstract: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. Existing multimodal memory methods largely focus on storing and retrieving records, with limited mechanisms for learning from completed tasks and consolidating task-specific experience. We therefore propose MMMem, a task-aware multimodal memory framework that extracts and consolidates experience from completed tasks through four complementary strategies. First, source-linked multi-view memory organizes original text, images, and rendered pages alongside generated scene images that combine clues across records for retrieval. Second, source-generated tasks support knowledge alignment at two levels: warm-up consolidates source knowledge into task-relevant experiences in external memory, while self-training adapts the model's parametric knowledge to task demands. Third, the same vision-language model distills completed tasks into experiences that record the task context, conclusion, and support links. Finally, task-aware retrieval recalls source views and relevant experiences for answering and verification, while source-supported reuse guides long-term retention. Across three memory benchmarks and two vision-language readers, MMMem outperforms eight baselines. With Qwen3.5-9B, MMMem achieves relative gains of 36.9%, 17.6%, and 15.2% over the best-performing baselines on LoCoMo, Mem-Gallery, and LooGLE v2, respectively. Ablations show consistent gains from training and memory warm-up, while case studies illustrate how individual components work in practice.

papers.title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
papers.abstract: Trustworthiness is a crucial issue for generative AI, as modern models can produce convincing and confident responses even when their outputs are incomplete, unsupported, or wrong. The frequent absence of ground-truth knowledge or labels complicates verification of generative AI outputs. To address this issue, we propose a trustworthiness framework grounded in model-internal confidence calibrated against an external expert reference. We estimate per-token trustworthiness of a student generative model as the statistical typicality of each generated token relative to an expert model's distribution, where the expert is used as a distributional reference rather than as a source of factual verification labels. To this end, we introduce an AI ontology calibrator that leverages the student model's internal latent features and token-level output statistics to compute expert-reference acceptance scores. Combined with traditional token-level confidence, entropy, and perplexity statistics, calibrator scores yield a compact set of $15$ response-level indicators for correctness classification. Evaluated across BF program generation, mathematical problem solving, and medical question answering, combined calibrator and traditional indicators provide complementary reliability signal which could be used to build detectors of untrustworthy outputs and hallucinations. Remarkably, our experiments show that these detectors are transferable across domains, although transferability is not always symmetric.

papers.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
papers.abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.

papers.title: Interpreting the $γ$-Ray Emission of the Cygnus X region with a Combined Cygnus OB2 and Cygnus X-3 Scenario
papers.abstract: The recent detection of high-energy $γ$-ray emission up to PeV energies from the Cygnus X region points to the presence of a PeVatron therein. This region hosts notable candidates such as the Cygnus OB2 association, which may be associated with PeV $γ$-photons detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO). The X-ray binary Cygnus X-3 also lies along the line of sight to the Cygnus X region, and LHAASO has observed modulated PeV $γ$-ray flux from its direction, indicating that its contribution is also non-negligible. Here, we attempt to interpret the $γ$-ray emission of the Cygnus X region using a combined scenario. Assuming a hadronic origin, we consider contributions from Cygnus OB2, Cygnus X-3, and Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs). Our results show that Cygnus OB2 alone, or its combination with the GCR component, is insufficient to account for the multiwavelength observations, whereas including the $γ$-ray emission from Cygnus X-3 naturally explains these observations. This suggests that the $γ$-ray emission from the Cygnus X region has a more complex origin, necessitating a joint consideration of Cygnus OB2 and Cygnus X-3. The expected neutrino flux from hadronic interactions extends into the GeV band and can help reveal the radiation mechanism of Cygnus X-3, underscoring the need for high-sensitivity GeV neutrino observatories.

papers.title: AdvMTO: Multimodal and Temporal Adversarial Object Attacks via 2D Gaussian Splatting for BEV-Based 3D Object Detection
papers.abstract: Adversarial object attacks pose a threat to BEV-based 3D object detectors in autonomous driving. Existing attacks typically target a single modality, coordinate camera and LiDAR observations at the current timestamp, or model temporal persistence mainly in camera streams. Without a unified construction of current and historical observations, attacks can leave part of the detector's accumulated evidence unsuppressed, limiting their effectiveness. In this paper, we propose AdvMTO, a 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) framework for suppressing detection of persistent adversarial objects. Its oriented surfels encode appearance, geometry, and opacity in one object state, from which camera images and scanline LiDAR returns are generated. AdvMTO then constructs current and historical inputs through detector-native processing, regenerating LiDAR returns in each native source sweep for fusion detectors. We optimize bounded appearance perturbations for each detector, propagating gradients through historical BEV memory for temporal camera detectors. For fusion detectors, bounded geometry refinement along local normals further perturbs both sensing modalities. Experiments on nuScenes demonstrate effective suppression of traffic-cone detection across three BEV detectors. Temporal ablations further highlight the importance of detector-native history modeling for both attack construction and optimization.

papers.title: Backward Error and Scaling in Level-Based ILU(k) and IC(k) Preconditioners
papers.abstract: We analyse the effect of rounding errors and diagonal scaling on level-based ILU($k$) and IC($k$) preconditioners. Because the sparsity pattern is fixed in advance, the computed factors are those that the incomplete factorization produces, in exact arithmetic, for a nearby matrix, and the deviation of the preconditioned matrix from the identity is bounded by an incompleteness term plus a rounding term. When no shift or pivot modification is needed, scaling leaves the iterates unchanged in exact arithmetic but can change the quantities in this bound by orders of magnitude. For IC($k$), we bound the change in the preconditioned eigenvalues caused by rounding by a multiple of the Skeel condition number of the incomplete factor, which does not depend on the scaling, and we show that after Jacobi scaling the entries of the factor are bounded, so that in half precision a breakdown can be detected before any overflow. Experiments in double, single and half precision illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks
papers.abstract: Post-training large language models routinely pools reasoning trajectories from diverse teachers or algorithms, yet it remains unclear whether standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can learn such heterogeneous strategies without explicit mode conditioning. We study the learnability and local bottlenecks of heterogeneous reasoning through a formal mixture formulation and controlled experiments. We first formalize the representational compatibility of the optimal autoregressive model with latent reasoning mixtures: the target next-token distribution weights modes by their prefix posteriors and concentrates on a single mode once alternative modes assign negligible likelihood to the prefix. In a verifiable symbolic graph-search environment with paired breadth-first and depth-first search trajectories, no consistent disadvantage is observed for unlabeled mixed SFT relative to homogeneous or labeled baselines under matched token budgets while preserving both modes. Scaling across 0.6B--14B models and data budgets largely eliminates global mode confusion, shifting the primary bottleneck to local state-tracking transitions. Because a local mistake affects the final outcome only when subsequent reasoning is sensitive to that step, we find that only a small fraction of local errors are outcome-determining \emph{Critical Reasoning Nodes (CRNs)}, and that single-step repairs at these nodes rescue failing trajectories across symbolic search and natural language benchmarks whenever the model has sufficient downstream competence to complete the remaining derivation. Our environment is open-sourced at https://github.com/Bowen1911/Symbolic_graph_env.

papers.title: Evaluating Persona Consistency in LLM User Simulators Without External Reference Annotations
papers.abstract: Standard evaluations assess LLM-simulated personas against an external ground truth, such as community trait annotations, but that reference is unavailable when the persona is inferred only from a short, task-oriented chat. We ask how persona consistency can be evaluated without such a reference, and propose a self-anchored internal-consistency diagnostic: the persona describes itself once and acts twice. A Likert self-report supplies a soft internal anchor; two behavioral profiles come from constrained scenario choices scored without a judge and from open-ended responses judged by an LLM. Consistency is the correlation between the self-report and each behavioral profile, in a shared six-facet BFI-2 space. The framework compares persona-construction strategies by assessing how consistently their elicited responses reflect their self-reported traits. Across ordinary-user chats (WildChat and LMSYS) and well-documented personas with community annotations (the Personality Database, PDB), profile-enriched representations agree with the anchor more closely than a raw-dialogue baseline. On PDB, this self-anchored ordering reproduces the community-annotation ordering. The pattern is stable across answering and judge models.

papers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Classiffcation of Relay-Surface Scattering Regimes for NLOS Millimeter-Wave Sensing
papers.abstract: In non-line-of-sight (NLOS) millimeter-wave sensing, relay-surface scattering alters target echoes and can cause propagation-model mismatch, angle-estimation errors, and ghost targets. DEKL, a deep-learning framework, identifies the dominant scattering regime from radar echoes without measuring surface roughness. Multipath echo models describe specular reflection, structured multipath reflection, and diffuse scattering. These models and a no-target hypothesis define a model-selection problem with unknown parameters. The Kullback-Leibler information criterion yields an adaptive decision rule for selecting among these hypotheses. A lightweight network, KLNet, learns covariance-domain features and combines attention with confidence-gated iterative decoding to avoid repeated likelihood evaluation. Analytical simulations, independent electromagnetic simulations, and radar measurements show that DEKL improves discrimination over the evaluated information-criterion-based rules. Ablations show how attention, confidence supervision, and gated decoding contribute to selective prediction and robustness under controlled covariance perturbations. The predicted regime guides propagation-model selection for radio-environment repre-sentations in wireless-network digital twins and informs NLOS localization and imaging.

papers.title: RigidAnchor: Cross-View Geo-Localization for UAV via Iterative Planar Rigid Alignment
papers.abstract: A UAV that flies without GNSS has to estimate its absolute position and heading without any external signal. Most existing methods for UAV-to-satellite cross-view geo-localization (U-S CVGL) treat the task as image retrieval: they compress the UAV image and each satellite tile into separate descriptors, rank the tiles by their similarity, and return the center of the best tile. The output can therefore only lie on a pre-defined grid, its accuracy is limited by the tile size, and no heading is produced. Regressing the pose in a single pass removes the grid, but it leaves no chance to correct the estimate afterwards. We observe that satellite tiles are not independent samples. They are laid on the map at a fixed spacing, scale and orientation, so neighboring tiles join into one continuous satellite block with a consistent metric, and a nadir UAV view of that block differs from it by a planar rigid transform only, i.e. a 2D translation plus an in-plane rotation. We therefore reformulate U-S CVGL as solving for this transform between two images of different sizes. Position and heading then become parts of one geometric quantity, and the accuracy is no longer limited by the tile grid. We propose RigidAnchor, which solves the transform iteratively. The network encodes the two images and builds a multi-level correlation pyramid between them. At each iteration, it indexes the pyramid with every aerial cell carried through the current estimate, pools the descriptors of all cells into one hidden state, and lets two decoupled heads predict a translation increment and a rotation increment, the latter being composed rather than added. On Bearing-UAV-90K, the cross-view mean errors are 78.6% lower in position and 69.7% lower in heading than Bearing-UAV, and HSR@15 increases by 19.06 points. Code is available at https://github.com/wwsource/RigidAnchor.

papers.title: A New Perspective on ANN-to-SNN Conversion: Hardware-Aligned Multi-Threshold Neuron Dynamics for Neuromorphic Inference
papers.abstract: By accumulating spikes over multiple timesteps, rate coding approximates the real-valued activations of an ANN, a principle that underpins numerous ANN-to-SNN conversion methods. However, the converted SNNs typically incur loss in accuracy compared to the original ANN. Existing methods either increase a number of timesteps or introduce more complex neuronal dynamics to reduce this accuracy gap. Yet, both approaches ultimately lead to the same outcome: redundancy either in information or in computation, thereby suffering from efficiency degradation. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{PRIME} (\underline{P}otential-\underline{R}esidual \underline{I}ntegration for \underline{M}ulti-threshold \underline{E}ncoding), a multi-threshold concurrent spiking neuron framework redesigned from a hardware data representation perspective:a) We introduce the Residual Membrane Potential Amplification (RMPA) mechanism, which replaces rate coding with Integration Coding by actively amplifying the residual membrane potential. RMPA enables the binary representation of spikes to carry substantially more information, achieving near-lossless conversion with as few as two timesteps.b) Complementarily, we implement concurrent spike firing in multi-threshold neurons, where spikes are decoded directly from the binary representation of floating-point data, eliminating membrane potential--threshold comparisons and replacing multiplications with lightweight bit-shift and accumulation operations that align with hardware computation primitives. At $T=2$ and $D=3$, we achieve competitive performance across both vision and language benchmarks with only 40.6\% of the FP32 bit-transmission cost and 13.4\% of the FP32 multiplication energy consumption. The PRIME framework establishes a new design principle for efficient ANN-to-SNN conversion, bridging the gap between algorithmic efficiency and hardware constraints.

papers.title: Apparent thermal conductivity governed by interface-injected phonon spectra
papers.abstract: Thermoreflectance techniques such as time- and frequency-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR and FDTR) are widely used to measure the thermal conductivity of bulk materials, thin films, and interfaces. When phonon mean free paths $Λ_ω$ become comparable to the thermal penetration depth, a Fourier analysis yields an apparent thermal conductivity $κ_{\rm app}$ that deviates from the bulk value $κ_{\rm bulk}$. Recent studies have highlighted the role of the phonon spectrum injected through the transducer interface, which is generally out of equilibrium owing to frequency-dependent transmission, and have shown that accounting for this nonequilibrium distribution can yield $κ_{\rm app}>κ_{\rm bulk}$, unlike conventional suppression-function analyses that predict only $κ_{\rm app}\leqκ_{\rm bulk}$. However, the spectral characteristics governing whether $κ_{\rm app}$ is enhanced or reduced remain unclear. Here, we resolve the surface-temperature response of semi-infinite Si mode by mode and show that short-$Λ_ω$-weighted injection raises the surface temperature, whereas long-$Λ_ω$-weighted injection lowers it. This behavior is governed by how deep the injected phonons travel before thermalizing with the lattice, which is set by their mean free paths, and by how effectively the substrate conducts the injected energy away, which is limited by its long-mean-free-path phonons. For an Al (70 nm)/Si structure, Fourier fits of synthetic TDTR phase signals give $κ_{\rm app}$ of Si from about 93 to 360 W/(m K) for different interfacial transmission spectra, and $κ_{\rm app}$ correlates with the heat-flux-weighted $Λ_ω$ of the transmitted phonons. Thus, $κ_{\rm app}$ from thermoreflectance reflects not only the substrate thermal properties but also the phonon spectrum injected across the transducer interface.

papers.title: Parallelizing Complex Matrix Multiplication: The 3M Solution
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing the product of two matrices with complex entries, a kernel used in quantum chemistry, electromagnetic simulation, quantum circuit simulation, and FFT-based methods. Standard practice already restructures the local computation using the classical \emph{3M} (Gauss/Karatsuba) identity, computing the product from three real matrix multiplications instead of four, dropping arithmetic by $25\%$ unconditionally but leaving communication unchanged. We show that whether 3M is worth doing at all, and whether it is additionally worth restructuring communication to get more of it by computing the three products \emph{in parallel} on disjoint processor groups, are independent questions, and we answer each in closed form under a standard $α$-$β$-$γ$ communication model. Under this model, for 2D layouts, in the large-$P$ limit, parallelizing the split reduces bandwidth by $13.4\%$ and latency by $1-1/\sqrt3\approx42.3\%$, the latter independent of the underlying algorithm's arithmetic exponent; neither reduction is achieved for 3D. For Strassen's algorithm the arithmetic picture reverses: restructuring locally is $7.1\%$ \emph{worse}, not better. We further generalize to Toom-Cook-$k$, giving a closed-form condition, increasing in $k$, under which higher-order splits rescue 3D layouts entirely: for instance, $k=3$ already makes 3D favorable for classical matrix multiplication, where the ordinary $k=2$ split never does.

papers.title: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
papers.abstract: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Ampère equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.

papers.title: DUET: Dual-MDL Unsupervised Entropy-Trie Segmentation for Low-Resource Languages
papers.abstract: Morphological segmentation, the task of decomposing words into constituent morphemes, becomes particularly challenging under extreme data scarcity, a regime that can arise in language documentation and linguistic reasoning. This difficulty stems from existing approaches' reliance on annotated data, external resources, or recurring patterns that emerge only in larger corpora. To address this limitation, we propose Dual-MDL Unsupervised Entropy-Trie Segmentation (DUET), a deterministic unsupervised algorithm that decouples structural candidate generation from statistical candidate ranking. DUET combines branching entropy with recursive paradigm discovery to generate linguistically plausible candidate segmentations, then ranks them using a dual minimum description length (MDL) criterion: a corpus-level objective rewards morpheme reuse, while a construction-tree objective guards against over-segmentation. On the SIGMORPHON 2023 interlinear glossing shared task, DUET outperforms unsupervised baselines in Morpheme F1 under both the standard and simulated extremely low-resource settings, while providing broader candidate coverage. Augmenting prompts with DUET segmentations improves performance on a linguistic reasoning benchmark, yielding the best overall results among the evaluated segmentation methods.

papers.title: Lorentz-invariant fiducial decay selection for the ATLAS $H\to ZZ^{*}\to 4\ell$ STXS measurement
papers.abstract: ATLAS measurements of Higgs boson production-mode cross-sections and Simplified Template Cross Sections (STXS), $σ\cdot B$, in the $H\to ZZ^{*}\to 4\ell$ decay channel rely on selection factors that fold in a decay-side fiducial acceptance evaluated with Standard Model decay kinematics. In an effective-field-theory interpretation that acceptance depends on the Wilson coefficients themselves. We recast these production-side $σ\cdot B$ results into a single Lorentz-invariant fiducial (LIF) decay region defined by the $H\to 4\ell$ decay, absorbing the EFT-dependent fiducial acceptance into the signal parametrisation, while the remaining reconstruction-efficiency corrections are shown to be largely EFT-independent. Using the Higgs boson signal Monte Carlo simulation at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 165 fb$^{-1}$, the LIF acceptance in the Standard Model is found to be $A^{LIF}_{SM}=0.8546$, production-independent to 0.07% and stable across STXS bins to 0.19%. Less than 1% of the reconstructed signal events originate from outside the LIF region, and the reconstruction efficiency for events in the region changes by at most 6% over the probed ranges of the EFT Wilson coefficients, as in the fiducial phase space of the published analysis. Consequently, the existing inclusive STXS cross-section measurements can be rescaled to the corresponding LIF fiducial phase space, allowing for EFT interpretations without EFT-dependent corrections for the reconstruction efficiency.

papers.title: Offsets in gravitational wave burst timing in eccentric black hole binaries with stellar-mass tertiaries
papers.abstract: At present, the formation scenarios producing observed compact binary coalescences (CBCs) are relatively unconstrained. Such mergers are thought to occur efficiently in hierarchical triple systems, with three-body dynamics and stellar interactions from the tertiary inducing mergers in the inner binary. Deducing the presence of a tertiary in an observed gravitational wave (GW) signal from a merging binary would be a smoking gun for this specific formation scenario, offering constraints on the evolution of CBC progenitors and multiple star systems. We present a fast model for the effect of tertiary perturbation on observed GW signals from generically-oriented eccentric inner binaries. We apply the model to two populations of triples with merging inner binaries: (1) a group of wide triples whose inner binary was driven to merger through excitations of the inner eccentricity due to three-body dynamics and von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai (ZKL); and (2) compact triples with chemically homogenously evolving (CHE) inner binaries that merge after experiencing mass transfer from the tertiary companion. When viewed face-on, the expected offset in the burst arrival time for the compact (CHE) triples varies by orders of magnitude depending on the properties of the triple system, with the majority of systems having an offset between $10^{-2}$ to $10^2$ seconds. A smaller fraction of the population with the highest inner eccentricities show the largest offset at $10^3$ to $10^6$ seconds. For the wide (ZKL) systems, the vast majority experience negligible perturbation from the tertiary. With an inclination of $π/2$ with respect to the observer both the compact and wide triple populations are expected to have offsets on the order of $10^3$ to $10^4$ seconds.

papers.title: Revisiting Evidence of Temperature Fluctuations in H II Regions. I. Interionic temperature differences
papers.abstract: The oxygen abundance of H II regions is a fundamental tracer of chemical enrichment and gas cycling and is now routinely measured across a broad range of cosmic time. A persistent complication is the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF): the O$^{++}$/H$^+$ abundance inferred from optical recombination lines (RLs) is systematically higher than that inferred from collisionally excited lines (CELs). Small-scale temperature fluctuations within the O$^{++}$-emitting gas are among the most widely discussed explanations for this discrepancy. However, the recent identification of a substantial continuum-pumping contribution to the O II spectrum of M42 motivates a renewed assessment of which observations uniquely favor a temperature-based interpretation and which are also compatible with other mechanisms. In this first paper of a series, I examine the relation between the inferred temperature-fluctuation parameter, $t^2$, and interionic temperature differences, focusing on $ΔT_e=T_e([OIII])-T_e([NII])$. Photoionization calculations show that ionization stratification naturally produces systematic temperature differences between the low- and high-ionization zones. Meanwhile, the conversion from an ADF to $t^2$ is strongly temperature dependent because CEL emissivities are nonlinear functions of electron temperature. I show that these two effects can account for much of the observed $t^2$-$ΔT_e$ relation without requiring the interionic temperature difference itself to trace fluctuations within the O$^{++}$ zone. This result does not exclude temperature fluctuations in H II regions. Instead, it indicates that interionic temperature differences should be interpreted with care and, on their own, provide limited discrimination among proposed origins of the ADF.

papers.title: CHIP: Contrastive Hardware-Image Projection. Can OpenAI CLIP Reconstruct Images from the CPU Computational Footprint?
papers.abstract: Image inference on a shared CPU leaves input-dependent traces in software-visible performance counters and execution time. CHIP (Contrastive Hardware-Image Projection) trains a lightweight residual projector on public images to map these measurements into the 768-dimensional visual embedding space of a frozen OpenAI CLIP model. A frozen Stable unCLIP generator uses the projected embeddings to reconstruct recognizable color scenes for held-out inputs. The attack requires no physical probe, candidate image gallery, domain-specific generator, or shared cache, and elapsed time alone retains the signal. We evaluate full-counter, single-counter, and timing-only measurements on Intel Haswell and Sapphire Rapids. The projected embeddings achieve 0.85 ROC AUC for held-out image identification, compared with a 0.50 baseline. Exact-image top-five retrieval reaches 24% on CIFAR-100 and 56% on Unsafe-Diffusion. Across both processors, reconstructions average $1.4\times$ the baseline RGB color-palette overlap and $2.5\times$ the baseline structural similarity.

papers.title: Continuum Pumping Revises Metallicity in the Orion Nebula
papers.abstract: The enrichment of heavy elements in the interstellar medium is central to understanding galaxy evolution. Oxygen, the most abundant element after H and He, provides the principal tracer of gas-phase metallicity, typically measured using nebular emission lines in star-forming regions. However, a long-standing issue-the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF)-produces a $\sim 0.25$ dex offset between metallicities derived from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs). We present deep spectroscopic observations of the Orion Nebula (M42), and use them to assess the contribution of the often neglected continuum pumping process. We find that the continuum pumping effect is at least a factor of two stronger than previously expected. After accounting for the flux contribution from continuum pumping, the RL metallicity is consistent with the CEL metallicity, thus explaining the bulk of the ADF. Reassessing O/H measurements in five literature star-forming regions using the same method, we similarly find a systematic reduction of RL-based metallicities. These results indicate that RL metallicities, which have previously been considered more reliable than CELs, are subject to potentially large bias from continuum pumping. This study provides a foundation to correct this bias and establish accurate element abundance scales throughout cosmic time.

papers.title: OCCA-Seg: Object and Channel Context Aggregation for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images
papers.abstract: Semantic segmentation, which assigns a class label to each pixel, is a key task in computer vision. However, semantic segmentation of remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging because of complex scenes and objects at multiple scales, which limits segmentation accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a context aggregation scheme called object and channel context aggregation (OCCA), consisting of three components: object contextual attention module (OCAM), channel contextual attention module (CCAM), and aggregation module (AM). Firstly, motivated by the observation that each pixel shares the class label of the object to which it belongs, object-level context represents each pixel through aggregating context from its corresponding object class. Secondly, because feature channels are correlated with object categories, channel-wise context models channel-wise contextual dependencies conditioned on object categories. Finally, the context information from OCAM and CCAM are fed into AM and used to weight and modulate the object context, enhancing the discriminative ability of the segmentation model. The experiments on several public remote sensing datasets including LoveDA, UAVid, ISPRS Potsdam, and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate competitive improvements over existing methods.

papers.title: Computation in flight through precision-processed optical fiber
papers.abstract: In distributed sensing and computing systems, optoelectronic conversion, buffering, and scheduling can make data movement a bottleneck. We propose FBG-CA, a passive computing module fabricated by automated through-coating inscription of weak fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs). The spatially distributed FBGs reflect, delay, and accumulate temporal samples to produce a convolution output in the backward direction, while the forward signal carries the original data stream to a remote receiver. This enables transmission and convolution within the same optical propagation event. To mitigate finite reflectivity resolution and fabrication deviations, we combine quantization-aware training with sharpness-aware minimization. Over 1440 m of computing fiber, the single-wavelength implementation achieves a convolution correlation coefficient of 0.987, classification accuracies of 87.90% on MNIST and 79.07% on MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, and an estimated throughput of 288 GOPS. With approximately 20% forward-power reduction (0.97 dB) across the FBG sections, the recovered MNIST images achieve a mean structural similarity index of 0.9930, and the recovered MIT-BIH heartbeat waveforms have a mean squared error of 0.005826. Using four wavelength-division-multiplexed channels over 144 m of computing fiber, FBG-CA achieves 92.25% accuracy on four-class Fashion-MNIST and an estimated throughput of 115.2 GOPS. An architecture-level projection indicates an intrinsic throughput density of 1.6 POPS/m for eight wavelengths at 100 GBaud per wavelength. These results demonstrate passive, wavelength-scalable computation-in-flight in optical fiber.

papers.title: SGPC: Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint for Stable Off-Policy Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Off-policy safe reinforcement learning (RL) faces a challenging trade-off between task optimality and constraint feasibility. In primal-dual methods, the coupled optimization of cumulative reward and constraint penalties through adaptive Lagrange multipliers may induce oscillatory policy updates near the safety boundary and amplify the effect of unreliable reward estimates outside the safe set. To address these issues, we formulate a new constrained optimization problem (COP) for safe RL by introducing a Safety-Guiding Policy (SGP) and a corresponding Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint (SGPC). The proposed COP augments the standard COP in safe RL with a conditional safety-guidance constraint. During actor updates, the current actor is evaluated using the learned cost critic. If it is predicted to be outside the safe set, SGP provides a nearby lower-cost training reference, and SGPC guides actor optimization toward this reference. Once the policy enters the safe set, the added constraint becomes inactive, and the formulation reduces to the original COP. This formulation leads to a plug-in actor-training constraint that can be integrated into off-policy safe RL algorithms. By applying primal-dual optimization to the auxiliary COP, we finally derive an SGPC-based off-policy safe RL algorithm and implement it in two representative off-policy algorithms, yielding SAC-SGPC and TD3-SGPC. Experiments on multiple Safety-Gymnasium benchmarks demonstrate that SGPC achieves a better optimality-safety trade-off by substantially reducing constraint violations and cost oscillations while maintaining competitive or better task returns.

papers.title: Skill-Adaptive Noise Scheduling for Diffusion Policies
papers.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion policies have demonstrated strong effectiveness when integrated into hierarchical skill-based learning frameworks, leveraging offline data to capture multimodal and temporally abstracted behaviors. However, prior approaches have rarely considered the diffusion process as a learnable component, adopting fixed noise schedules applied uniformly across skills, regardless of their distinct behavioral contexts. Such a design fundamentally limits the achievable performance, particularly for contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks where different skills exhibit distinct couplings between action dimensions. In this paper, we present a skill-adaptive noise diffusion framework (SaND) which introduces a learnable, skill-conditioned noise schedule that modulates the diffusion process per action dimension, adapting the noising dynamics to each skill. To prevent the learned noise schedule from collapsing into trivial solutions, we employ an auxiliary inverse objective that reconstructs the skill embedding from the Legendre coefficients of the derivative of the noise schedule, encouraging the schedules to remain skill-discriminative. This formulation naturally enables adaptive control over the denoising steps for each skill, where noise schedules are clustered in the Legendre coefficient space, and the appropriate number of denoising steps is determined at the point where reconstruction error abruptly increases. At inference, we identify each skill embedding's cluster from its noise schedule and apply the corresponding number of denoising steps, dedicating more compute to skills requiring fine-grained control and less to simpler ones. In simulation and on real robot hardware, SaND outperforms existing skill learning and planning baselines on contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks, achieving higher success rates while requiring fewer denoising steps.

papers.title: A response-based self-energy from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory and its reduction to GW, GW+SOSEX, and GF2
papers.abstract: We construct a frequency-dependent one-particle correlation self-energy by coupling a reference Green's function to the neutral excitation response obtained from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory with singles and doubles (EOM-CCSD). Direct, mixed direct-antisymmetrized, and fully antisymmetrized choices of the external interaction vertices define three approximations, all admitting an explicit spectral representation without numerical frequency integration. In the bare-state limit, the mixed and fully antisymmetrized forms recover second-order Green's-function theory (GF2), whereas the direct form retains only its ring contribution. With a direct random-phase approximation (RPA) response, the direct and mixed forms reduce to $G_0W_0$ and $G_0W_0$ plus second-order screened exchange (SOSEX), respectively. For molecular ionization potentials, replacing the RPA response by EOM-CCSD generally lowers the ionization energies, whereas introducing exchange at one external vertex raises them. These substantial opposing effects partially compensate, although the mixed approximation does not systematically improve upon conventional $G_0W_0$, either against IP-EOM-CCSD or QUESTDB reference energies (aug-cc-pVDZ mean absolute errors relative to the QUESTDB theoretical best estimates: 0.45 vs 0.36~eV). A third-order perturbative analysis reveals that the three approximations retain different contributions and weights of particle-hole diagrams while omitting explicit particle-particle and hole-hole ladder contributions and the static self-energy. In particular, the fully antisymmetrized form recovers GF2 at second order but assigns incorrect weights to its retained third-order diagrams. These findings highlight the importance of a balanced treatment of screening and vertex corrections in constructing accurate self-energy approximations.

papers.title: Principal spectral theory of time-periodic nonlocal advective cooperative systems and its applications
papers.abstract: We develop a new spectral theory for time-periodic nonlocal cooperative systems with advection on bounded intervals, allowing asymmetric dispersal kernels. By transforming the problem into a nonlocal moving-boundary problem, we show that the associated Poincaré map is strongly positive and power compact, which yields existence and uniqueness of the principal eigenvalue and several variational characterizations. For spatially homogeneous coefficients, we establish the limit of the principal eigenvalue as the interval expands to $\mathbb R$ and identify it as the minimum of the principal Floquet exponents of the associated exponentially weighted periodic systems. To the best of our knowledge, this spectral theory is new even in \textbf{the scalar case}. We then apply these results to nonlinear systems. On bounded intervals, the sign of the principal eigenvalue gives a sharp dichotomy: solutions either converge to a unique positive time-periodic solution or vanish as time tends to infinity. We also prove convergence of positive periodic solutions as the interval expands. For the Cauchy problem on the whole real line, we characterize the leftward and rightward spreading speeds, which may differ for asymmetric dispersal kernels, and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for accelerated spreading in either direction. In particular, under irreducible coupling, accelerated spreading in one component induces accelerated spreading in all components in the same direction.

papers.title: Sierpiński Gaskets Julia set and Postcritically finite fractals
papers.abstract: Devaney's work on the Julia sets of the McMullen family, established these rational maps as central objects in holomorphic dynamics. For Misiurewicz parameters, that is when the orbits of the critical points are all strictly preperiodic to a repelling cycle, the topological point of view taken by Kameyama links the dynamics of such rational maps to that on the attractors of invertible self-similar iterated function system. Eroğlu, Rohde, and Solomyak showed that in favorable cases the topological conjugacy is in fact quasisymmetric. We survey the machinery underlying these results and propose directions for further research.

papers.title: Privacy-Enhanced Distributed Sensing Network via Causal-Order Switching and Probe Squeezing
papers.abstract: As sensor networks become more interconnected, sensitive information sharing among multiple users poses potential risks of information leakage, making privacy protection a critical challenge. To address this challenge, we quantify network privacy using the maximum information leakage ratio (MILR) and propose a protocol that enhances privacy through causal-order switching and probe squeezing. Causal-order switching harnesses intrinsic network propagation dynamics for privacy encoding, while probe squeezing suppresses information leakage through quantum channels and increases the information available for estimating the global parameter. These mechanisms enable an asymptotic exponential enhancement on the privacy with the squeezing rate. We experimentally demonstrate this mechanism in distributed beam-tilt sensing using spatially structured light without requiring nonclassical light sources. Our work identifies intrinsic network propagation dynamics as a resource for privacy protection and opens a new avenue for continuous-variable sensing networks that combine high precision with enhanced privacy.

papers.title: Attributing Security Outcomes in LLM-Agent Evaluations: The Role of Content-Free State
papers.abstract: Security benchmarks for LLM agents record whether each attack succeeded and compare agents, attacks, and defenses by attack success rate (ASR). Such comparisons are valid only if the agent, the attack, and the defense cause each verdict. We show that verdicts also depend on content-free state: details of a run that carry no information about the system under test, such as the Python hash seed, the order of tools or evidence, and the scoring of failed runs. We require that this state influence no verdict (decision noninterference) and treat it as untrusted input, because evaluators and requesters of LLM-based gates can choose it. Our framework, TARE (Testing Attribution of Reported Effects), attributes a reported effect to the agent, attack, or defense only if it exceeds the measured influence of content-free state. On Agent Security Bench (ASB), runs with a fixed hash seed are identical for seven agents from four model families, yet changing the seed changes up to 17% of an agent's verdicts while the ASR moves by at most 5 points. The seed acts through the tool order: sorting the tool list instead of reverse-sorting it raises the ASR by up to 19 points, because ASB's naming convention places attacker tools first. When the same evidence is reordered, six of seven LLM judges change their decision on 17-91% of 98 proposed actions. Across eighteen agent-defense combinations, TARE's worst-case test attributes effects to two of three defenses, one of them in opposite directions on two agents, and a test fixed in advance confirms a 4.8-point decrease from the third; in the attributed decreases, 35-69% of the stopped attacks end without any tool call, which ASB counts as a failed attack. Reproducible verdicts are thus not necessarily attributable, and security evaluations of LLM agents should report the influence of content-free state. We release TARE, the ASB patch, and all verdict tables.

papers.title: Segre Classification as a Framework for Generating Exact Solutions in Static Cylindrical Spacetimes with Levi-Civita Matching
papers.abstract: The main objective of this article is to analyze cylindrically symmetric static spacetime based on the Segre classification, where each Segre type corresponds to a set of canonical forms of Ricci spinors represented by Newman-Penrose scalars. The surviving Segre types of trace-free Ricci tensor in the cylindrical geometry are $[1,(111)]$, $[1,1(11)]$, $[(1,1)11]$, $[1,111]$, $[(1,11)1]$, $[(1,1)(11)]$ and $[(1,111)]$. Different combinations of eigenvalues and eigenvectors formed via Segre classification aid in understanding the distribution of matter and energy within that particular kind. Solutions are presented for the isotropic type $[1,(111)]$, for the anisotropic type $[1,1(11)]$, where a new metric function is introduced, and for type $[1,111]$, where all three pressures differ and the Krori-Barua functions are used. They satisfy the physical and stability criteria, namely the Zeldovich condition, causality condition, energy conditions and adiabatic index. The types $[(1,1)11]$ and $[(1,11)1]$ have $ρ=-P_r$ and give dark energy like configurations in which the strong energy condition is violated in the core, the latter having the tachyonic fluid form of the energy momentum tensor. For type $[(1,1)(11)]$, a charged solution in the presence of a non-null electromagnetic field is obtained and joined to an electrovac exterior. Matching with the Levi-Civita exterior shows that the vanishing of the radial pressure at the boundary is equivalent to the Darmois conditions. The C-energy and the curvature invariants are evaluated for each solution, and the results are compared with earlier works.

papers.title: Stellar Temporal Intensity Interferometry with Adaptive Optics at the Palomar Observatory
papers.abstract: Spatial intensity interferometry has seen a major resurgence in astronomy due to its immunity to atmospheric phase turbulence, but its temporal counterpart - a cornerstone of quantum optics - has remained largely unexplored for astronomical sources. Here, we demonstrate that high-visibility temporal photon bunching signatures from stellar sources are now accessible by combining ultra-narrowband spectral filtering with high-speed single-photon counting detectors. Leveraging the adaptive optics architecture at the Palomar Observatory, we report the first observation of resolved stellar temporal photon bunching, with a peak of $g^{(2)}(τ=0) = 1.3 \pm 0.1$, from the red supergiant $α$ Her. This advance establishes stellar temporal intensity interferometry as a viable observational modality, bridging quantum optics with high-resolution stellar astrophysics.

papers.title: How long must an honest confidence interval be after causal discovery? Benign and malignant weak edges
papers.abstract: After causal discovery, a confidence interval for a total effect valid uniformly over the model class must pay for structural uncertainty. We measure this price by the worst-case ratio of expected length to that of the efficient interval knowing the graph, for linear Gaussian models with a known superset of the adjacencies and k-triangle faithfulness. The global price is of order sqrt(n) once one edge can be malignant, so we study it locally, near a generic distribution with one edge absent. Our main result classifies this weak edge by Meek closures. It is benign if deleting it leaves the effect identifiable in the resulting MPDAG and Markov equivalent explanations agree; the local price is then bounded, and otherwise, for small k, of order sqrt(n). At benign edges the price is of order R+K, with R a ratio of efficient lengths and K a cross-model constant. It equals one, so that honesty is free, exactly when K = 0, generically decided by a d-separation. For two Markov classes it is determined within a factor 3.40, and its upper bound is approached without knowing the base point or the weak edge. A further graphical condition gives the rate uniformly in a second edge's margin.

papers.title: Operator-Valued Q-Learning: Compositional Bellman Recursions for Order-Sensitive Decision Making
papers.abstract: In quantum pulse sequences, spacecraft attitude control and in-hand reorientation, actions act on a hidden physical state as non-commuting operators, so the outcome of a plan depends on the order of its actions. We let the value function carry this structure: each Q(s,a) is an N x N operator, and the Bellman backup applies the action's dual map to the continuation value, Q(s,a) = K_a^*(R(s,a) + gamma E V(s')). Unrolled along a plan, the recursion builds the ordered product of the actions' operators, and the value at any latent state is a linear trace readout. It is exact for policies that do not observe the latent, the backup contracts for unitary and orthogonal dynamics, and an asynchronous operator TD scheme learns it with almost-sure convergence. Classical values live in a lattice, so a maximum over actions exists; self-adjoint operators form an anti-lattice (Kadison) and have none. An operator log-sum-exp still gives one operator per state-action pair whose readout upper-bounds the value of every policy at every latent state. The sampled update converges to it for a finite horizon, and it reduces to soft Q-learning and the QMDP bound when actions commute. We prove that scalar values on observations that ignore action order must confuse swapped histories, that exact history tables grow exponentially for free action groups but polynomially for nilpotent ones, and give a Hankel-rank lower bound on the operator dimension. In experiments the learned policy matches 1000-simulation tree search on SO(3) pointing for horizons up to 20 at ~10^4 times lower decision cost, transfers zero-shot to unseen initial states, and acts exactly on its belief mean when the initial state is hidden, where plugging the mean into a DQN does not. A planner with the same model knowledge is more sample-efficient at short horizons, and a DQN given the operators matches or exceeds OpQ.

papers.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
papers.abstract: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent, Innata-0-Agent, coordinates long-horizon execution through memory, verification, and recovery. A co-design protocol is further proposed to align model training with agent execution and leverage validated experiences to support subsequent adaptation and model improvement. Extensive evaluations demonstrate strong embodied capabilities across understanding, world prediction, and robotic manipulation. Innata-0 represents our first step toward physical intelligence, and we see it as the beginning of a much longer journey.

papers.title: Voyag: Joint Multi-Intent Detection and Execution-Relation Classification for In-Vehicle Voice Assistants
papers.abstract: An in-vehicle voice assistant must decide not only which intents an utterance contains but also how co-active intents may be executed: concurrently, in a fixed order, or not at all without arbitration. We present Voyag, a single-forward decision model that jointly predicts ten controlled vehicle-intent slots and a three-way execution relation (parallel, sequential, mutually exclusive) over each co-active intent pair. Voyag combines a multilingual ModernBERT-style encoder (mmBERT-base, 306.9M parameters), a typed per-slot choice head, and a lightweight GroupCalibration relation head (1.61M parameters) that consumes marker hidden states, pooled context, explicit resource-requirement profiles, and symmetrized outer-product conflict features. All objectives are optimized in one joint loss: soft cross-entropy over slot choices, focal cross-entropy over relations, and a mutex-consistency penalty. On a synthetic Chinese vehicle-life benchmark with semantic scene-level splits and a leakage audit (30,017 / 3,473 / 5,000 groups), validation-only selection yields 0.9893 slot accuracy and 0.0526 expected calibration error over 50,000 slot decisions. Conditioned on gold intents, the relation head reaches 0.8548 accuracy, 0.8473 macro-F1, and 0.6062 mutually-exclusive recall over 4,000 pairs; end to end with one encoder forward it reaches 0.8530 accuracy and 0.8464 macro-F1. Against a two-stage rule pipeline, the aggregate end-to-end gain is small and borderline, so we claim no aggregate advantage; the learned head's advantage lies in sequential and parallel recall where surface rules are blind. We report rule baselines with a tautology disclosure and a held-out thermal conflict failure.

papers.title: StutterStigma-TR: A Novel Turkish Dataset and Target-Aware BERT Framework for Stuttering-Related Stigma Detection
papers.abstract: Computational research on disability-related ableist harm remains limited, and condition specific resources for stuttering-related stigma are particularly scarce. This study introduces StutterStigma-TR, a Turkish dataset of 6,019 public X/Twitter posts annotated as Stigmatizing, Non-stigmatizing/contextual, or Supportive using a speech and language therapy-informed protocol with independent lived-experience evaluation. We also propose StutterStigma-BERT, a BERTurk-based target-aware framework that combines explicit target marking, target-span representation, target-conditioned context, character-level and handcrafted orthographic information, and gated discourse cues. The framework is evaluated in complementary three-class and binary settings using controlled three-seed ablation analyses and final 20-seed robustness evaluations. Under the common training protocol, Gated Discourse-OrthoTarget trained with cross-entropy is selected as the final configuration for both tasks based on internal-validation Macro-F1. Across 20 random seeds, the final three-class model achieves a mean Macro-F1 of 73.54%, while the final binary model achieves 85.17% using validation-selected decision thresholds. Task adapted harmful-language comparators are additionally evaluated under the common training protocol, and the proposed model obtains the highest mean Macro-F1 among them. For the primary three-class task, matched backbone analyses show higher internal validation Macro-F1 with BERTurk than with TurkishBERTweet or Turkish Mamba, while substantial train-validation separation persists across all three backbones. Separate direct-transfer and zero-shot experiments examine performance without StutterStigma-TR supervision. Across the task-adapted, direct-transfer, and zero-shot comparisons, the condition-specific supervised systems retain the strongest aggregate performance.

papers.title: Existence and multiplicity of radial solutions for higher order logarithmic and infinite mass Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the Schrödinger equation $-Δu+V(x)u=g(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$, where $V$ is radial and $g(t)/t\to-\infty$ as $t\to0$. In this infinite-mass case the energy functional is not finite on $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. First let $g(t)=t|\log|t||^{α-1}\log|t|$ with $α>1$. We only assume that $V$ is continuous and bounded from below. So $V$ may change sign, and it need not be coercive or have a limit at infinity. We obtain a nontrivial radial solution and a sequence of radial solutions whose energies tend to infinity. To do this, we add the term $λ|u|^{p-2}u$ with $1<p<2$, find critical points of the perturbed functional by minimax methods, and let $λ\to0$. The infinite-mass structure gives the compactness in this limit. Next let $g$ be odd, with a power bound near zero and at most critical growth at infinity. Let $V$ be bounded, with a smallness condition on $(x\cdot\nabla V)_+$. We combine the Pohozaev identity with an augmented symmetric minimax method and obtain infinitely many pairs of radial solutions. A negative critical power term is allowed.

papers.title: What Field Enumeration Costs to Compile in C++26: Native Reflection, Structured-Binding Packs, Reflection Libraries and Hand-Written Serializers on GCC 16
papers.abstract: C++26 adds standard ways to enumerate a struct's fields, among them static reflection (P2996, with P3394 annotations) and structured-binding packs (P1061), alongside hand-written code, X-macros and libraries (Boost.PFR, reflect-cpp, Glaze) that now ship pre-C++26 and C++26 paths. We time each in a struct serializer with byte-identical output on GCC 16.2.0, at the front end and at -O2, in randomized interleaved rounds with code-level checks of every single-factor contrast. At the front end, inline native enumeration in the form used in several of P2996's own examples, an expansion statement over the std::span of define_static_array, costs about as much per struct of 16 scalar fields as Boost.PFR and 7.96x a P1061 pack, itself about as cheap as hand-written code. The same loop over a constant array costs 0.47x as much: about half of the span form's cost comes with the span. The ratio to P1061 shrinks on a heterogeneous type graph and at -O2. In a whole translation unit at the front end the library outweighs the mechanism: 200 structs take 0.59 s with inline native enumeration, 0.56 s with Boost.PFR and 3.86-4.13 s with the C++26 paths of reflect-cpp and Glaze, whose visitors also compute field names. Per type, each library's C++26 path is cheaper than its pre-C++26 path at 16 fields, but Glaze's gain reverses at 128 fields (pinned release v9.1.0); Boost.PFR's C++17 path grows almost quadratically with the number of types. Hand-written serializers sharing one overloaded name grow superlinearly with the number of types. The -freflection flag alone makes reflection-free code up to 1.264x costlier per type on GCC 16.2.0 and up to 2.578x on 16.1.0, so comparisons between mechanisms depend on the point release. Part of the span form's cost grows with the number of structs, which we trace to GCC registering block-scope statics in quadratic time (reported as GCC PR128928).

papers.title: BiLight: A Fast Method for Estimating Counts of 6-Vertex Bipartite Motifs in Large Graphs
papers.abstract: Motifs, or small subgraphs, are fundamental building blocks of complex networks. Analyzing their frequency distribution provides deep insights into the local structure of graphs, with applications in social network analysis, bioinformatics, and web mining. However, exact enumeration of motifs becomes computationally expensive as the size of the motif and the network increases. This challenge is particularly acute for bipartite motifs, which are ubiquitous in modeling relationships like user-item, author-paper, and actor-movie interactions. In this work, we present BiLight (Bipartite Lightweight motif estimation), a scalable framework for estimating the frequencies of all 17 non-isomorphic 6-vertex bipartite motifs. Specifically, we focus on estimating the non-induced counts of these motifs, which is a common requirement in many graph mining tasks. Our approach relies on a randomized path sampling of paths on four vertices. We use an efficient, weighted strategy by counting the ways that each sampled path can be extended to one of the 17 motifs. This framework yields unbiased estimates of the global motif counts. We conduct extensive experiments on networks of various sizes. Our experiments demonstrate that BiLight converges rapidly to the ground truth with high accuracy, even on massive networks where exact counting is infeasible. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/celikmustaa/BiLight.

papers.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
papers.abstract: Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques. As a first application of our theorem, we obtain \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)>2^{Ω_k(n\log n)}\). Combined with the upper bound due to Mubayi and Suk, this yields \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)=2^{Θ_k(n\log n)}\), where \(B^{(k)}\) is the half-graph. This answers in the affirmative a question posed by Mubayi and Suk. As a second application of our theorem, we show $r_k(k+1,3;n)=2^{Θ_k(n^{k-2}\log n)}$, which, together with a new stepping-up lemma developed in this paper, further yields $r_k(k+1,t;n)=\twr_{t-1}(Θ_{k,t}(n^{k-t+1}\log n))$ for every fixed $k\ge6$ and $4\le t\le k-2$, where $\twr_1(x)=x$ and $\twr_{j+1}(x)=2^{\twr_j(x)}$. Here $r_k(k+1,t;n)$ denotes the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the $k$-subsets of an $N$-vertex set contains either $k+1$ vertices spanning at least $t$ red edges or a blue clique of order $n$. As a third application of our theorem, we show that $r_k(F_{\ell,k,d},n)>2^{Ω_{k,\ell,d}(n^{k-d-2}\log n)}$ for all fixed integers $k\ge4$, $1\le d\le k-3$, and $\ell\ge2k+1$ with $k\nmid\ell$, where $F_{\ell,k,d}$ is obtained from the $k$-uniform tight cycle of length $\ell$ by deleting $d$ consecutive edges.

papers.title: Software-Engineering-as-an-Artifact: From Engines to Systems That Build Themselves
papers.abstract: Software engineering (SE) is evolving rapidly as generative AI and LLM-based agents grow more capable. Yet, as a community, we risk using these new tools to solve problems that a changing SE process may no longer pose. We consider how AI may transform, and in part already is transforming, both the SE process and the systems it produces. Drawing on scenario planning methods from futures studies, we extrapolate from observed trends to a deliberately extreme scenario in which the SE process fully materializes in artifacts (like context documentation and executable skills). Such a process would culminate in SE engines that autonomously produce and update systems directly from requirements and user requests. The work of human engineers would then shift from the product to the process: they would maintain the artifacts of these engines, while the engines produce and evolve the software. We probe this scenario in scenario-validation interviews with four SE industry practitioners. The interviewees found the scenario largely plausible and desirable, and two reported that parts of industry are already moving this way; one questioned whether tacit engineering knowledge can ever be fully captured in artifacts. Even if this end state is reached only in part, we argue that reasoning about it can inform the intermediate stages. SE research should therefore take such futures into account when choosing its research directions.

papers.title: Stability and bifurcation of shrinking spheres for the fractional mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We study the fractional mean curvature flow near shrinking spheres. The first shape eigenvalue changes sign at \(s_*(n)=(\sqrt{n^2+6n+1}-n-1)/2\). Above this threshold, sufficiently small perturbations of a sphere become extinct at one point, and their extinction rescalings converge exponentially to the round shrinker. Below the threshold, the sphere is nonlinearly unstable modulo translations and dilations. We also construct smooth, strictly convex, nonspherical homothetic shrinkers bifurcating from the spherical family near the threshold. In the plane, the noncircular branch bifurcates on the side \(s>s_*(2)\).

papers.title: Growing Knot Embeddings into Spherical Graphs
papers.abstract: Knotted structures occur throughout soft matter and biology, where topological constraints can shape relaxation and spatial organization. Here, we introduce a computational construction that maps a specific 3D knot embedding to a graph embedded on the sphere through growth and interfacial-energy relaxation. For standard 3D embeddings of prime knots with at most seven crossings, we obtain a family of growth-based graphs that generally differ from the corresponding Tait graphs. We further identify an empirical growth-graph reconstruction rule based on polygonal regions with alternating crossing structure in a knot diagram. Non-minimal diagrams demonstrate that these graphs are not knot invariants, while selected connected sums suggest that graph features associated with their prime factors can remain recognizable. Determining how these graphs transform under isotopy may reveal invariant features, which we leave for future study.

papers.title: MASTO: Missed-thrust Aware Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. Therefore, in this work, we utilize a stochastic hybrid system framework to model a spacecraft as a Markov jump system that can switch between nominal and failure mode. We formulate the Missed-thrust resilient trajectory optimization problem as a Markov jump covariance steering problem, and propose a sequential convex programming-based approach, which can also respect chance constraints. We demonstrate our framework on two complex three-dimensional transfers in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three body problem, showcasing robustness against a range of MTEs, while respecting chance constraints. We further analyze controller performance across a range of MTE-probability distributions, offering valuable insights into the MTE-resilient trajectory design trade space.

papers.title: Can Search Agents Correct Their Own Errors? Evaluating Retrieval, Evidence Delivery, and Answer Completion
papers.abstract: A search agent can leave an earlier error unresolved by missing the right source, overlooking a relevant passage, or failing to revise and deliver the answer after receiving the evidence. We evaluate these possibilities on BrowseComp-Plus by replaying each model's own wrong closed-book answer in conversation and intervening on what evidence reaches the model. In a supplied-evidence study spanning four open-weight checkpoints, 709 questions and 26,665 test conditions, a confident assistant prior reduced Nemotron's paired accuracy by 16.1 percentage points despite answer-bearing passages in context. When the user insisted on the prior, accuracy fell by 32.9 points for Nemotron and 12.6 for gpt-oss. Among gpt-oss responses that lost correctness in that condition, abstention was more common than repeating the prior. In separate search interventions with Qwen3.5 and Nemotron, placing a gold page first often left the decisive source unopened. Delivering a decisive passage in context improved accuracy over neutral delivery by 51.0 percentage points for Qwen3.5 and 22.4 for Nemotron. Even with the passage in context, Nemotron exhausted its search budget and returned no answer in 19 of 51 episodes. The tests distinguish failures of retrieval, passage delivery, correction and answer completion, giving system builders a way to test which changes resolve a recurring error.

papers.title: The type-II double copy for relativistic Rindler fluids
papers.abstract: Within the Weyl double copy framework, we study a mixed single-copy construction for the Petrov type-II geometry of first-order relativistic Rindler fluids. Working on a common fixed flat Rindler background with consistent spinor conventions and a real field strength representation, we algebraically factorize the Weyl spinor into two symmetric rank-two Maxwell spinors and test the Maxwell equations and the zeroth copy scalar equation up to the first order in the relativistic gradient expansion. We separate the degeneration parameter from the gradient expansion parameter and analyze the continuous degeneration to the Petrov type-D and type-N branches as the complex shear and vorticity tend to zero, together with the preservation of the accuracy of the Maxwell and scalar field equations along each path. We also compare the relativistic construction with the nonrelativistic case.
